purpose: Executable traceability manifest from every semantic-modeling audit finding to a focused current acceptance contract or explicitly named future acceptance scaffold. The final closeout card must update each future_acceptance_scaffold to current_acceptance when its owning implementation card lands.

findings.invariant: Ordinary Rust construction, generated builders, and Serde rehydration must enforce the same aggregate relationships; public field products must not manufacture impossible reservations, messages, workflow events, documents, vaccine records, incidents, approvals, staff tasks, or invariant-bearing scalar values.

successor_implications.implication: Close Reservation public construction and add compile-fail field privacy coverage.
Close Message lifecycle construction and distinguish approval evidence from queue authority.
Close WorkflowEvent and WorkflowOutcome relationship construction.
Close Document, VaccineRecord, Incident, ApprovalRecord, and StaffTask aggregate construction.
Audit every invariant-bearing Deserialize implementation against equivalent constructors.
Replace lossy collections and untyped rehydration errors where arbitrary products still compile.
Use trybuild only where compile-time protocol/field-privacy guarantees are real.
Move mixed ownership from omnibus entity surfaces into canonical semantic modules.

findings.invariant: Completion, value attribution, and review lifecycle evidence are not executable approval authority. Only explicit approval evidence may create approved review rows, outbox candidates, or authority-bearing capabilities.

successor_implications.implication: Replace completion booleans with evidence-bearing review disposition values.
Keep finance/value attribution evidence independent from approval/completion state.
Separate historical message approval evidence from executable queue authority.
Move repository/outbox authority into app-owned workflow ports rather than API shell shortcuts.
Introduce opaque, target-bound authority capabilities only after explicit approvals.
Review every projection for accidental authority from booleans or status strings.

findings.invariant: A vaccine review packet accepts exactly one coherent approve/reject decision; repeated, conflicting, or unknown packet decisions are typed conflicts that do not panic or silently overwrite document, vaccine, eligibility, approval, or audit state.

successor_implications.implication: Replace the current approve boolean path with a typed vaccine review decision protocol and conflict errors.
Make VaccineRecord and ApprovalRecord construction enforce temporal/review coherence.
Map repeated/unknown review packet failures into the unified public error envelope.
Security review must prove no panic path remains for malformed review packet ids.

findings.invariant: Mutating HTTP routes must derive actor identity, role, and location from trusted runtime context; request-body actor ids are claims for cross-checking, never authorization grants.

successor_implications.implication: Introduce app-owned authenticated actor context and route authorization seam.
Vaccine review decisions must consume trusted actor context, not body-only staff ids.
API shell stays routing/conversion only; app ports own authorization and mutation.
Authentication and authorization failures use the canonical safe public error envelope.
Independent security review must check all mutating routes, not only vaccine review.

findings.invariant: Public HTTP contracts are NVA-owned versioned DTOs with stable identity; handlers must not leak provider DTOs, duplicated ad hoc metadata, known-schema untyped Value blobs, or boolean protocol metadata where semantic modes are known.

successor_implications.implication: Adopt apps/api::public_contract DTOs directly in handlers and snapshot their serialized shapes.
Remove storage record vocabulary from handler bodies where app ports exist.
Use one public error envelope for all route families.
Review public DTO identity against provider DTO quarantine.

findings.invariant: SpacetimeDB reducers and read models project typed, versioned storage rows and codecs; they must not encode approval gates, source refs, outcomes, actor identity, or blocked actions as booleans, debug strings, comma-joined lists, or lossy labels that cannot round-trip.

successor_implications.implication: SpacetimeDB actor rows remain trusted context inputs, not body claims.
Reducers call app-owned ports rather than becoming domain/application owners.
Resolved by typed review-gate/source/actor/outcome/blocked-action columns, exhaustive codec tests, and checked claim/recommendation/disposition/manager/capture transitions.
Persist fallible typed conversions for ids, refs, timestamps, statuses, and JSON payload versions.
Reducer failures map to typed safe errors.
Cross-layer review must inspect realtime projection fidelity.

findings.invariant: Every promoted provider/storage fact attaches source provenance, mapping version, and adapter boundary evidence before app/domain use; provider DTOs remain quarantined and never become product truth by shape alone.

successor_implications.implication: Serde promotion tests must distinguish raw DTO/row types from validated domain values.
App ports receive source-backed values rather than raw API/storage records.
Implement explicit source-backed promotion values for Gingr customer, pet, and retail mappings.

Resolved by private Postgres rows plus explicit fallible promotion for source refs, versions, IDs, timestamps/periods, money/currency, idempotency keys, workflow/topic codes, and relationship-checked JSON payloads.
Independent review must classify remaining provider promotion gaps by fixture availability.
Final closeout must prove every manifest entry resolved, superseded, or explicitly inapplicable.
